name: The Threshold of Machine Authorship
title: The Threshold of Machine Authorship
answer: The threshold of machine authorship is the line between human creative or inventive contribution and output generated by a machine. It covers copyright registration, patent inventorship, database rights, and contract terms that assign or disclaim ownership. The question is not whether AI can make things, but whether a person or company can claim legal authorship over what it makes. The site tracks 149 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how central this threshold has become.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: The threshold of machine authorship is the line between human creative or inventive contribution and output generated by a machine. It covers copyright registration, patent inventorship, database rights, and contract terms that assign or disclaim ownership. The question is not whether AI can make things, but whether a person or company can claim legal authorship over what it makes. The site tracks 149 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how central this threshold has become.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Machine authorship runs on generative models, training data, prompts, human editing, version histories, metadata, and model logs. The infrastructure includes text and image generators, code assistants, and the platforms that host them. It also includes the records that show how an output was produced, such as prompt logs, model versions, timestamps, and edit histories. The site lists 732 AI tools, many of which produce or modify content. Provenance standards and watermarking systems are part of this layer.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners compare the human contribution against the machine contribution. They review prompts, revisions, selection, arrangement, and creative control. They look at registration practice and case law to see how tribunals and courts treat authorship. The site tracks 29 AI case law precedents, which are used to map that treatment. They also draft agreements, disclosures, and internal review steps.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The threshold affects ownership, infringement, moral rights, disclosure, record keeping, and liability. It determines who can enforce rights, who bears risk, and what must be disclosed to registries, clients, and platforms. Provenance records are used to show human contribution and to trace training data or generated elements. The site has 222 compliance and regulation pages, reflecting the volume of rules that touch this area.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect more registration guidance, more disputes over human contribution, and more contract terms. State legislatures are active, with 7066 state AI bills tracked on the site, though not all address authorship. Courts and agencies will likely refine tests for sufficient human control. Provenance and disclosure requirements may become standard in publishing, software, and media workflows. The threshold may shift from a binary to a graded test.
